title: Particulate nature of matter
competency: Demonstrate that matter is made up of tiny particles that are always moving.

keywords.def: A tiny piece of matter, too small to be seen.
The idea that matter is made up of tiny particles.

ideas.name: Matter is made of tiny moving particles

en.text: All matter is made of tiny particles with spaces between them. The particles are too small to see. They are always moving. A balloon keeps its shape because gas particles fill it. Wind moving leaves and dust shows that particles move.

screens.title: Inside a balloon
screens.ask: You blow up a balloon. What fills it and keeps its round shape?
opts: Tiny gas particles we cannot see
screens.after: The balloon is full of tiny gas particles. We cannot see them, but they push on the rubber.

screens.title: 2.1.2 Particulate nature of matter
paras: The particle model says all matter is made of tiny, moving particles.
There are spaces between the particles.
The particles are too small to be seen.

screens.title: What the activity shows
paras: An inflated balloon is filled with small particles of gas.
The gas may be helium, hydrogen, oxygen or air.
Wind blows leaves and dust around.
This shows particles of matter are in continuous motion.
The idea that matter is made of tiny particles is the particulate nature of matter.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A tiny piece of matter, too small to be seen.
The idea that matter is made up of tiny particles.

opts: Tiny particles that are always moving
screens.ans: Tiny particles that are always moving
screens.why: This is the particulate nature of matter.
screens.clue: Think about the balloon and the moving dust.

screens.why: All matter is made of tiny particles.
screens.clue: Choose from the word box: particles, moving, energy …

screens.why: The particles of matter move all the time.
screens.clue: Think of dust in the wind.

screens.text: The particles in hot water have ___ energy than particles in cold water.
screens.why: Hot water got more heat. Heat is energy, so its particles move faster.

screens.text: The particles in ice move less than the particles in liquid water.
screens.why: In ice the particles only vibrate in place. In water they slide past each other.

screens.text: A drop of perfume is opened in a corner. Soon the whole room smells. Which idea explains this best?
opts: Perfume particles move and spread out
The smell is a form of light
screens.ans: Perfume particles move and spread out
screens.why: The perfume is made of tiny particles. They keep moving, so they spread through the air to every corner.

items.why: All matter is made of particles.
items.clue: Word box: increase, less, faster, cold, temperature, water, particles, moving, more, energy.

items.ask: An increase in energy makes particles move ___.
items.why: Adding heat (energy) makes particles move faster.

items.ask: An increase in ___ is the same thing as an increase in energy.
items.why: When a substance gets hotter, its particles gain energy.

items.ask: The particles in hot water have more energy than ___ water.
items.why: Hot water has more energy than cold water.

items.ask: The particles in ice move ___ than particles in water.
items.why: Ice particles only vibrate in place.

test.text: Matter is made up of tiny particles that are too small to be seen.
test.why: This is the particulate nature of matter.

test.text: Why does an inflated balloon keep its shape?
opts: It is filled with gas particles
test.ans: It is filled with gas particles
test.why: Gas particles fill the balloon and push on it.

test.text: Wind blows dust around. What does this show?
opts: Particles of matter are always moving
test.ans: Particles of matter are always moving
test.why: The book uses wind and dust to show continuous motion.

test.ask: An increase in energy makes particles move ___.

test.text: Kebede heats water from 20 °C to 60 °C. What happens to its particles?
test.why: Heating adds energy, so the particles move faster.
